colorRules.accentUsage: Use the deep teal accent as a focused action color for primary CTAs, selected navigation states, focus-visible rings, links, progress indicators, and concise financial status highlights. Keep it intentional and limited to roughly 3-7 appearances per screen. Prefer accent-600 or accent-700 for filled actions, with lighter accent steps reserved for subtle selection backgrounds, badges, and hover states.
colorRules.semanticUsage: Use semantic colors functionally and sparingly: success for positive account activity, completed transfers, and healthy financial progress; warning for upcoming bills, low balances, or actions needing review; danger for failed payments, fraud concerns, and destructive actions; info for neutral guidance and educational money tips. Prefer soft semantic background tints with readable semantic text and restrained borders; do not use semantic colors as decoration or as competing primary accents.
colorRules.neutralUsage: Use the pale blue-green background neutral for the app canvas, raised neutral surfaces for primary panels and controls, and overlay neutrals for dialogs or layered UI. Use the darkest neutral for primary text and headings, mid-dark neutrals for supporting copy and labels, muted neutrals for metadata and helper text, and light neutral steps for subtle dividers and borders. Maintain clear hierarchy through tonal contrast rather than heavy shadows or multiple saturated colors.
forbiddenPatterns: Do not use more than one accent hue in a screen or introduce generic electric blue, indigo, or purple as a secondary brand accent.
Do not use the teal accent as a large decorative page wash, full-screen background, or ornamental illustration.
Do not use gradients on cards, app sections, dialogs, or other surfaces.
Do not use pure black or pure white; preserve the soft blue-green neutral atmosphere.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate financial status; pair semantic color with labels, icons, or values.

typographyRules.displayUsage: Use Sora for brand expression, page titles, dashboard headings, prominent balances, and short navigation labels where a confident fintech voice is useful. Its geometric shape should make money management feel clear and approachable without turning the interface into a toy.
typographyRules.bodyUsage: Use DM Sans for all body copy, form labels, inputs, table content, transaction descriptions, helper text, and practical navigation details. Keep copy conversational, direct, and easy to scan for people building financial confidence.
typographyRules.monoUsage: Use JetBrains Mono only for technical or precision-oriented content such as account IDs, transaction references, API values, masked routing details, or tabular numeric comparisons. Do not use it for general body copy or prominent marketing headlines.
typographyRules.weightRules: Use 600-700 for Sora headings and key balances, with 700 reserved for the strongest page-level emphasis. Use DM Sans 400 for body copy and transaction details, 500 for labels and navigation emphasis, and 600 for buttons, totals, and critical values. Avoid weights 200, 300, 800, and 900; never bold entire paragraphs.
typographyRules.sizeRules: Use 16px/24px as the minimum for body copy, inputs, and primary transaction content. Use 12px/16px only for compact metadata, timestamps, and auxiliary captions. Use 14px/20px for secondary labels and dense table support, 18-20px for emphasized supporting text, 24-30px for section headings, and 36-48px for page titles or prominent financial balances. Keep heading lines short and avoid oversized type that overwhelms practical app content.

spacingRules.sectionMargins: Use a centered max-width container of approximately 1280px with app-first sidebar and content structure. Separate major dashboard regions with 48-96px vertical spacing depending on importance, using up to 128px only for exceptional page-level transitions. Vary section spacing intentionally rather than repeating identical blocks.
spacingRules.componentPadding: Use 16px horizontal and 12px vertical padding for compact rows, controls, and transaction items. Use 24px horizontal and 16px vertical padding for relaxed panels, forms, and summary modules. Reserve 32px padding for high-priority surfaces or spacious empty states. Keep touch targets comfortably sized and align padding to the tokenized rhythm.
spacingRules.rhythmDescription: Use an airy but practical 4px foundation with a strong 8px rhythm. The balanced density should favor clear transaction scanning, generous row separation, and restrained panel padding rather than dense spreadsheet compression or excessive whitespace. Use whitespace to group financial decisions and reduce cognitive load.

motionRules.transitions: Use opacity for non-essential reveals, color and border changes for hover, focus, selected, success, and warning states, and small translate or scale transforms only for buttons, menus, and layout changes that benefit from spatial feedback. Animate balance or transaction updates subtly and never make financial information feel unstable.
motionRules.easing: Use the standard cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) curve for smooth, controlled movement. Motion should feel crisp and responsive rather than bouncy or ornamental, matching the brand's bold but minimal personality.
motionRules.duration: Use 120ms for hover, pressed, focus, and other micro-interactions; 200ms for dropdowns, tabs, validation, row state changes, and component transitions; and 320ms for page-level reveals, panel entry, and meaningful layout changes. Respect reduced-motion preferences and remove non-essential transforms when requested.

signatureMoves: A deep-teal action system that makes the next financial step obvious without saturating the entire interface.
Prominent financial balances and totals set in Sora, paired with calm DM Sans transaction detail for an approachable contrast between confidence and clarity.
Structured transaction rows and account summaries that use tonal neutral surfaces, concise labels, and restrained semantic status markers instead of card-heavy dashboards.
Small playful moments through short conversational microcopy and crisp state feedback, while keeping the underlying layout disciplined and trustworthy.
A soft blue-green canvas with raised near-white surfaces and thin cool borders, creating a recognizable calm fintech environment without gradients or visual noise.
antiPatterns: Do not use centered marketing-hero composition, footer navigation, or tab-bar navigation in the desktop app; use a functional sidebar with content-first layouts.
Do not build the dashboard from a grid of more than three cards per viewport; prefer transaction lists, tables, and grouped rows.
Do not use rainbow financial status colors, decorative accent blocks, or saturated illustrations that compete with balances and actions.
Do not use oversized playful typography, all-caps body copy, slang-heavy messaging, or jokes that undermine financial trust.
Do not use carousel testimonials, floating blobs, ornamental dots, gradient surfaces, or gratuitous motion.
